title: Samlor Korko / សម្លកកូរ
description: A hearty Khmer stew with vegetables, fragrant kroeung and toasted rice.
ingredients: Catfish or pork belly (300g, cut into chunks)
Long beans, cut into sections (1/2 cup)
Moringa or bitter gourd leaves (1 cup)
instructions: Prepare aromatics. Heat oil in a deep pot and fry prahok with green kroeung paste until fragrant.
Sear meat. Add fish or pork chunks and stir thoroughly until coated in the fragrant paste.
Simmer soup. Pour in water or broth, bring to a simmer, then add green papaya, pumpkin, and long beans.
Thicken and finish. Stir in toasted roasted ground rice and fresh moringa leaves. Simmer for 5 minutes and serve warm.

title: Nom Banh Chok / នំបញ្ចុក
description: Rice noodles with a fragrant fish curry, fresh herbs and crisp vegetables.
ingredients: Yellow kroeung paste (lemongrass, turmeric, galangal, 4 tbsp)
Fresh mint and basil leaves (1/2 cup)
Prahok and palm sugar (1 tbsp each)
instructions: Pound fish paste. Simmer freshwater fish in water, debone, and pound finely with yellow kroeung paste.
Simmer curry broth. Heat coconut cream gently in a pot, add the pounded fish-kroeung mixture and stir.
Season broth. Add broth, prahok, and palm sugar; simmer on low heat for 20 minutes.
Assemble and serve. Place rice noodles in bowls, top with crisp banana blossom, cucumber, herbs, and warm broth.

title: Num Ansom / នំអន្សម
description: Sweet banana sticky rice, steamed in banana leaves.
ingredients: Palm sugar and pinch of salt
Fresh banana leaves and bamboo twine for wrapping
instructions: Prepare sticky rice. Soak rice for 4 hours, drain, and mix with coconut milk, grated coconut, and palm sugar.
Wrap parcels. Place sticky rice on banana leaves, lay a banana in the center, and cover with more rice.
Tie tightly. Wrap the banana leaves securely around the rice and bind firmly with bamboo twine.
Steam parcels. Steam or boil in a large pot for 1.5 to 2 hours until the rice is tender and fragrant.
